newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude broadly firmer despite wild card Brent.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude broadly firmer despite wild card Brent.

text.p: Most North Sea crudes strengthened on Friday, helped by a surge of refinery demand which soaked up at least six million April barrels but benchmark Brent lagged behind amid uncertainty over the fate of six cargoes held by Shell, traders said.
"The grades have definitely improved big time today but it's possible that those Brents will be dumped back on the market next week," said a trader.
Norwegian Oseberg gained 10-15 cents to trade at Dated Brent -15 cents and UK Forties saw its discount narrow by a similar amount to trade at Dated Brent -5 cents.

Traders said Forties was benefitting from the cancellation of six April cargoes because of lower than expected production at one of the system's fields but robust refining margins and a deep contango were also helping push values higher.
"It's beginning to pick up, partly because storage is working for some and because margins are healthy," said one.
But Dated Brent was struggling with some traders expecting Shell to sell up to six Brent cargoes back into northwest Europe next week, partly to benefit a short CFD position.
The major was exploring arbitrage opportunities to the U.S. but traders doubted whether the economics would work.
May Brent was steady at $18.18 a barrel and intermonth spreads were also unmoved, May/June trading at -22 cents and June/July at -11 and -10 cents.
Brent CFDs picked up a couple of cents as next week's dates traded at June Brent -92 cents but activity was slow with dealers unwilling to anticipate Shell's next move.
"Dated Brent will probably trade lower than the CFDs next week but it won't be as low as May -95 cents," said a trader.
Two Brent turning wet on Friday were kept by trader Arcadia and a third by British Petroleum, dealers said.
